key_insight: Africa-Papers introduces a 10.15-billion-token academic corpus designed to improve African representation in foundation-model training.
clinical_relevance: Its African medical scholarship could support more locally relevant medical NLP, but clinical benefits are not demonstrated in the abstract.
method: Combines DOAJ journals, CGIAR CGSpace, African-focused arXiv preprints, and OpenAlex-indexed publications.
Converts full texts into layout-aware Markdown preserving sections, equations, and tables.
Adds exact BPE token counts and a standardized eight-domain taxonomy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 844,807+ full-text papers across 879 Parquet shards, with DOAJ coverage spanning 31 African nations, but no downstream model evaluation.
watch_item: Corpus scale alone does not establish medical accuracy or equitable coverage; downstream performance needs local validation.
paper_title: Africa-Papers: A 10-Billion-Token Multi-Domain Academic Corpus for African Foundation Language Models
